sections.title: Part Ⅰ TASK A. Readback and Hearback

body.label: Tower
body.text: HL123, line up and wait runway 16, number two for departure.

body.label: Tower
body.text: HL123, after departure turn left heading 130, climb to 11,000 feet, contact Departure on 125.75.
BRIMO

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, when 30 miles from BRIMO descend to 10,000 feet, reduce speed to 250 knots.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, descend to 2,500 feet, cleared for the ILS runway 16 approach, report established.

sections.title: Part Ⅰ TASK B. Checking, Clarifying, Confirming, Informing

body.text: Your company minimum for a visual approach is 5,000 metres visibility and a 2,500 foot cloud base. The latest report gives 8,000 metres and a cloud base of 4,000 feet. Listen to the controller, respond with a reason, and tell him both the reported visibility and the figure your company requires.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, are you able to accept a visual approach to runway 21?

Earlier the controller told you to maintain 250 knots. Ten minutes later the same controller said "no speed restriction, resume normal speed", and you have been at 300 knots since then. Now ATC contacts you. Respond accordingly.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, confirm maintaining 250 knots?

While descending through 7,000 feet you lost about 15 knots of airspeed very suddenly and the aircraft sank. It lasted a few seconds, you were hand-flying, and you did not say anything about it at the time. You are now level at 5,000 feet. Acknowledge the instruction, and report what you met on the way down.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, turn right heading 240 for vectors to the ILS.
Approach gave you the altimeter as 29.78. You set 29.87 by mistake and have only just noticed it. You are level at 6,000 feet indicated. Now ATC contacts you. Respond accordingly.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, say your altitude.

You are in continuous moderate turbulence at flight level 330. Your turbulence penetration speed is 280 knots and you are at 280 knots now. Listen to the controller, respond with a reason, and tell him both speeds.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, increase speed to 320 knots for spacing with the traffic behind you.
Weyland Departure / transition altitude

sections.title: Part Ⅱ TASK A. Role-play & Follow-up

pre.text: Flight Paths In this scenario, you'll be the pilot flying HL123, which goes through 3 flight stages: Taxi, Departure, Climb.

Initial Situation You are the pilot of HL123 at Gate Charlie 4 at Weyland Airport, ready for departure to Ferndale Airport. You have 3 hours 10 minutes of fuel on board and the flight plan says 2 hours 20 minutes to Ferndale.

body.text: Weyland Delivery / Ferndale / TULAN TWO departure
Contact Weyland Delivery and request your ATC clearance.
TULAN TWO departure / BRIMO transition
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Delivery
body.text: HL123, cleared to Ferndale via the TULAN TWO departure, BRIMO transition, climb to 7,000 feet, squawk 2514.
Listen to the ground controller, give a full readback, and acknowledge the delay.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, Weyland Ground, taxi to holding point Charlie 2 via Golf and Lima. Bravo's closed for resurfacing, so it's the long way round — about 8 extra minutes. Sorry about that.
Golf / Lima / Charlie 2
Listen to the ground controller, report your position from the picture, and say which holding point you are taxiing to.

body.label: Ground
body.text: HL123, say your position — are you on Golf now, or have you already turned onto Lima?
Listen to the tower and give a full readback.

body.label: Tower
body.text: HL123, Weyland Tower, behind the departing Boeing 777, line up and wait runway 16, wind 140 at 8.

pre.text: Situation Update You are airborne from runway 16 and now passing 3,000 feet for 7,000 feet.

body.text: Make an initial contact with Weyland Departure and report your passing altitude.

pre.text: Situation Update Passing 12,000 feet a fuel imbalance warning comes up — the right tank has 900 kilos more than the left. The checklist tells you to open the crossfeed and to stop the climb at flight level 250 until the imbalance is corrected, which takes about 25 minutes. Your flight plan cruise level is flight level 370.

body.text: Listen to the controller, respond with a reason, and tell him both levels.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, Ridgeway Control, climb to flight level 370.
Listen to the controller and answer both parts of his question.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, say again — what level can you accept, and how long do you need?
Ferndale / Crestview
Listen to the controller, state your decision with a reason, and tell him both fuel figures.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, at flight level 250 your fuel burn will be higher — the company flight plan now gives 2 hours 45 minutes to Ferndale from here. Crestview is 40 minutes away if you'd rather. I'll leave that with you.
BRIMO
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Center
body.text: HL123, roger, maintain flight level 250, cleared direct BRIMO, contact Ridgeway Control on 133.45 in 10 minutes.
You have just finished Task A, as the pilot of Hotel Lima one two three.

In this situation, Ridgeway Control offered you Crestview but you continued to Ferndale at flight level 250. What did you compare before you decided, and why? In your role as a pilot, how do you work out whether you still have enough fuel when you are held down at a lower cruise level? Give an example of a situation where you would divert rather than continue.

sections.title: Part Ⅱ TASK B. Extended Role-play : Single Incident/Emergency Related

pre.text: Initial Situation You are the pilot of HL123, level at flight level 260 and 70 miles from ORVIL, inbound to Norgate Airport. You have 1 hour 40 minutes of fuel on board and you have information Tango.

body.text: Contact Norgate Approach and report your position.
ORVIL ONE arrival / ILS runway 21
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, Norgate Approach, descend to 10,000 feet, reduce speed to 250 knots, expect the ORVIL ONE arrival, ILS runway 21, Norgate altimeter 29.92.

pre.text: Situation Update Passing 14,000 feet the fuel quantity on the left side starts dropping much faster than the right. You have a fuel leak from the left wing. You have closed the crossfeed, so the leak is now taking fuel only from the left tank. You have 55 minutes of fuel left and your landing distance required is 2,200 metres. There is no fire.

body.text: Inform the controller of your situation, tell him what you have done about it, and request priority for landing.
Listen to the controller, respond with a reason, and tell him both figures — how long you can stay up and how long he needs.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, roger. I have one aircraft ahead of you — if I vector you round behind him it's 20 minutes to touchdown. Can you take that?
Listen to the controller and answer both parts of his question.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, say again — how many minutes of fuel do you have, and how many do you need?
Listen to the controller, give a full readback and say your intentions.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, understood. Turn right heading 310 for vectors to the ILS, descend to 6,000 feet. Say your intentions.
Listen to the controller and answer both of his questions.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, two things — do you want the fire service standing by, and is there any smoke or fire?

pre.text: Situation Update The leak has stopped. The fuel quantity on the left side is steady now and you have 45 minutes of fuel on board.

body.text: runway 21 / runway 03
Listen to the controller, state your decision with a reason, and tell him both distances.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, the aircraft ahead has gone around, so runway 21 will be blocked for about 6 minutes. Runway 03 is open now, but it's only 2,000 metres. What do you want?
Listen to the controller and give a full readback.

body.label: Approach
body.text: HL123, descend to 2,000 feet until established, cleared for the ILS runway 21 approach, contact Norgate Tower on 118.35.

sections.title: Part Ⅱ TASK C. Reporting about Task B

body.text: What happened to your aircraft (HL123)? Explain the nature of the incident.
How do you think the incident was handled by the air traffic controller? Do you feel the situation could have been handled differently? Make a comment from a pilot's point of view.
